newsitem.title: UK: IGC council meets, focus on improving grain supply.
newsitem.headline: IGC council meets, focus on improving grain supply.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) members gathered in London on Tuesday for a bi-annual council session, exchanging views on growing world supply.
The Council's Food Aid Committee met on Monday to review grain shipments to third world countries in the 1995/96 harvest season which ended in June.
IGC sources said total food aid was expected to have exceeded the agreed minimum requirement of 5.2 million tonnes of wheat equivalent.

But members expressed concern about a tendency by some donors to cut back on aid expenditure due to budget restrictions and the threat this could impose to their commitments under the IGC's Food Aid Committee.
"They shouldn't really be affected as there is a minimum requirement," commented one IGC official.

The London-based IGC -- representing importers and exporters -- projected a world wheat harvest of 580 million tonnes in 1997, five million tonnes higher than the estimate for this year despite an inclination by farmers to curtail sowings in the face of plummeting prices.

The grain supply situation has dramatically improved since farmers began to gather what has come to be a bumper harvest this year in many parts of the world only months after after tight stock situation caused global alarm.

The IGC said in its latest monthly report last week that the European Union could produce a big crop in 1997 after a bumper harvest this year but production decisions in Canada, Australia and Argentina would be largely affected by price levels.
It revised its estimate for coarse grains crops sharply up for 1996 to a new record of 884 million tonnes due to a large U.S. maize crop.
Officials said the council session was also assessing changes in national government policies and the impact of these on world grain trade.
